title: Rules of thumb
objectives: Answer out loud: Rattle off all five anchors.

blocks.body:
Memorize these until they're automatic:

| MOIC | Years | IRR |
|---|---|---|
| 2.0x | 3 | ~26% |
| 2.0x | 5 | ~15% |
| 2.5x | 5 | ~20% |
| 3.0x | 3 | ~44% |
| 3.0x | 5 | ~25% |

Rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ annual return. At 8%, ~9 years; at 12%, ~6 years.

legend.meaning: Works best for returns between about 6% and 12%

blocks.template: At 9%, money doubles in about {{1}} years (Rule of 72)

blocks.title: How do you estimate an unusual IRR, like 2.2x in 4 years?
blocks.body: Bracket it with anchors. 2x in 4 years ≈ 19% (between 26% at 3 years and 15% at 5). 2.2x is a bit higher, so roughly 22%. Exact: 2.2^(1/4) − 1 ≈ 21.8%.

blocks.prompt: Roughly what IRR is 2.2x in 4 years?
blocks.explanation: 2x in 4 years ≈ 19%; 2.2x is a bit higher, so ≈ 22% (exact: 2.2^(1/4) − 1 ≈ 21.8%).

blocks.title: Why do interviewers ask mental math?
blocks.teaser: To see whether you can sanity-check numbers quickly in a meeting without a spreadsheet, and how you stay composed under pressure.
blocks.body: To see whether you can sanity-check numbers quickly in a meeting without a spreadsheet, and how you stay composed under pressure. Think out loud.
